title: Same handbook, reshelved
spec: M04 · sections, order, and the data boundary
intro: One UCC extraction system prompt, 2,180 tokens, six sections. Shuffle nothing but their order and the model fabricates a debtor name. Put them back in priority order — same words, same bill — and it returns null with a flag.

provenance.source: a narrated re-architecture of one UCC extraction system prompt; token counts and prices are plausible inventions, not measurements

foot: The ordering here is M04's Order Is Meaning — identity and hard constraints at the top, bulk reference in the middle, the live task and its data fenced at the bottom.

steps.title: Take a census of the blob
narrative: The prompt in production is one 2,180-token string with no headings. Before changing a word, label every line by which of the six slots it belongs to: role, objective, rules, capabilities, output contract, examples — and note that the filing itself has been pasted in among them.

The census is the whole trick. "Write a better prompt" is an intimidating, unfalsifiable task. "Six named sections, each in the right place, with a boundary around the untrusted one" is an engineering task you can finish and check.
steps.youDo: Print your own system prompt with line numbers and tag each line with one of the six slot names. Anything you cannot tag is either dead text or a seventh thing you did not know was in there.

reference notes     600 tok   lines 2-13    <- at the top

steps.title: Ordering A — the critical rule in the crowded middle
narrative: Run it as-is on the amendment. Six hundred tokens of edge-case notes occupy the primacy slot at the top. The one rule that actually matters — never fabricate a debtor name; return null if it is not clearly in the filing — sits at line 14, in the most crowded and least attended stretch of the prompt.

The model returns NORTHBAY MARINE SUPPLY, INC. The rule was present. It was 180 tokens long, it was correctly worded, and it was in the wrong place. And because there is no delimiter, the filing's own text reads as one more paragraph of instructions.
steps.claudeSays: Nothing marked the boundary between your rules and the document. From where I sat, line 39 was just the next sentence.

terminal.text: fabricated — the never-fabricate rule was in the window at line 14

cells: the least important text holds the strongest slot
the non-negotiable, in the dilution zone

view.verdictNote: every required instruction was present; the answer is still invented

steps.title: Ordering B — same content, reshelved
narrative: Nothing is rewritten and nothing is added except sixteen tokens of angle brackets. Role and the hard rules go to the top in their own <rules priority="critical"> block. The 600 tokens of edge-case reference drop into the middle, which is the one place their bulk does the least damage. The output contract and examples follow. The filing goes last, inside <filing trust="untrusted">.

Same model, same call, 2,196 tokens instead of 2,180. The answer is null with ["amendment_reference"] — the honest result, and the one the downstream retrieval step can act on. The bill rounds to the same four decimal places.
steps.claudeSays: The prohibition is now the first thing in the prompt and the filing is now visibly a document. Neither of those is new information — both are new positions.
steps.youDo: Move your own hardest constraint to the top of its own delimited block and re-run your worst case before you change any of its wording.

terminal.text: no fabrication · contract honored · 2,196 tokens (+16 for delimiters)

lines: <role>You are a UCC Secretary-of-State filing analyst.</role>
- NEVER fabricate a debtor name. If not clearly in the filing, return null.
- Preserve the debtor name's EXACT capitalization as filed.
- Flag any name >= 80 characters as possibly truncated.
- UCC-3 amendments reference an original filing; the name may live there.
- Redacted debtors -> null with flag "redacted".      (600 tok, mid-prompt)

steps.title: The shelf order, and the seam it creates
narrative: Both ends of the prompt are privileged and the middle is the danger zone — which is why the old advice splits into "put the key instruction first" and "put it last" and both camps are half right. Architecting means deciding, per section, which end that section has earned.

The ordering pays a second dividend you get for free. Everything above the <filing> tag is byte-identical on every call in the pipeline, and everything below it changes per filing. That is exactly the seam M19 puts a cache breakpoint on — you built a cacheable prefix by ordering for attention, not for cost.

One more thing the census protects you from: contradiction by accretion. When rules live in one named block instead of accumulating across a paragraph, "always return JSON" and a later "explain your reasoning" end up adjacent, where a human can see them fight.
steps.youDo: Draw the line in your own prompt where stable content ends and per-call content begins. If those two are interleaved, you have both an attention problem and a caching problem.

needed, but rarely the thing that gets misapplied
the low-stakes zone; dilution does least damage here
close enough to the answer to shape it
the live task and its data, fenced
recency — and the boundary that makes it data

view.text: A system prompt is architecture, not prose. Name the six sections, order them by positional priority, state each rule exactly once, and put an explicit boundary between your instructions and anything you did not write. The same 2,180 tokens fabricated a name in one order and refused honestly in another — and the second version happens to have a clean stable/volatile seam — which is M05's trust floor and M19's cache breakpoint, both handed to you by an ordering you did for attention.
